findings.text: The tail of the CPU paravirt operations table groups page-table lifecycle and update hooks. It provides per-level allocation hooks taking a memory descriptor plus a frame number and matching release hooks taking only a frame number, then per-level install hooks for table entries, a two-phase modify-protection start and commit pair scoped by area and address, paired value extraction and construction helpers for each level, a lazy-mode flush hook, and a fixmap installer taking an index plus physical address and protection.

The patch template aggregates three operation groups, one each for CPU, interrupt and memory-management behavior, in that order, and requests a stable unrandomized layout so patch code can address members at fixed offsets.

Paravirt calls dispatch through an indirect call annotated as retpoline-safe, addressed through a memory operand naming the selected operation slot. The call wrappers emit volatile inline assembly with alternative patching so a native instruction sequence can replace the indirect call, always clobber memory and condition codes, preserve a platform call constraint, and pass up to four register arguments with distinct 32-bit and 64-bit argument and clobber assignments.

Return values narrower than a machine word are masked to their declared width after the call, and larger-than-word return types are rejected at build time. Void and value-returning forms share the same call skeleton, with alternate forms accepting an extra native sequence plus a feature condition, and callee-save forms addressing the function member of the wrapper.

Callee-save operations use a reduced clobber set relative to normal calls, with extra caller-saved registers listed separately on 64-bit. A generated thunk preserves all caller registers around a normal call: the 32-bit form preserves one register while the 64-bit form preserves a wider caller-saved set and restores in reverse order, bracketed by frame handling and placed in a selectable executable section under a derived raw name.
A negated Xen paravirt feature condition is exposed as a named alternative-patching predicate for selecting non-Xen native sequences.
The non-PCI parallel-port probe is a small wrapper that forwards its interrupt and DMA autodetection arguments unchanged to the ISA-port probe and returns that result.
PC configuration space uses an index port at 0x22 and a data port at 0x23, with the MPS IMCR selector valued at 0x70.
PC configuration bytes are accessed by writing the register selector to the index port first; reads then return the data port contents and writes then store the payload to the data port.

PCI BIOS services are numbered in the 0xB1xx family: presence query 0xB101, find by device 0xB102, find by class 0xB103, special cycle 0xB106, config read byte word dword 0xB108 through 0xB10A, config write byte word dword 0xB10B through 0xB10D, routing options 0xB10E, and hardware interrupt assignment 0xB10F.

Per-bus x86 PCI metadata stores a domain number and NUMA node unconditionally, with optional companion device, IOMMU private pointer, firmware node for message-signaled interrupts, and VMD parent device members enabled by configuration.

Bus helpers derive domain, procedural domain, node, firmware node and VMD membership from the bus private metadata. Domain and procedural domain agree, VMD is true only when a parent device pointer is present with a constant-false fallback configuration, all-bus assignment reports false, and early quirks are a no-op.
x86 PCI resource floors are 0x1000 for I/O, the platform memory-start variable for memory, and 0x4000 for CardBus I/O windows.
The platform advertises PCI mapping support with generic resource mapping, and write-combining mapping availability follows the page-attribute-table enabled state.

Node-to-CPU lookup has an unchecked inline form that directly indexes the per-node mask table and a checked NUMA form that validates the node id against the node count and the table entry for availability before returning it.

The checked node-to-CPU lookup warns with a backtrace on misuse: an out-of-range node yields the empty-CPU mask while a missing per-node table entry yields the online-CPU mask, so callers cannot distinguish those degraded results from genuine masks without checking the logs.
The PCI-bus-to-CPU lookup resolves the bus node and returns the online mask when the node is absent, otherwise the mask of that node.
PCI x86 debug output has two selectable forms: direct formatted printing, or a syntactically valid dead branch that evaluates nothing at run time.

PCI probing and behavior flags are bit values: BIOS 0x0001, config type one 0x0002, config type two 0x0004, MMCONFIG 0x0008, probe mask 0x000F, no-early 0x0010, then no-checks 0x0400, PIRQ mask 0x0800, assign ROMs 0x1000, BIOS IRQ scan 0x2000, assign all buses 0x4000, skip ISA alignment 0x8000, use CRS 0x10000, AMD MMCONFIG check 0x20000, IO ECS 0x40000, no ROM assignment 0x80000, root no CRS 0x100000, no BAR assignment 0x200000, big root window 0x400000, use E820 0x800000, and no E820 0x1000000.
Breadth-first PCI sorting control is a four-state enumeration in order: default, force off, force on, then firmware-table driven.

PIRQ routing data uses packed layouts without padding. Each slot entry carries bus and device-function identity, four link-plus-bitmap interrupt entries, a slot number and a reserved byte. The BIOS table adds signature, version, size, router location, exclusive IRQ mask, router identity, miniport data, reserved bytes, checksum and a trailing slot array; the compact table carries signature, provided and used counts, exclusive IRQ mask and a trailing slot array.
Routing tables depend on exact packed byte layout and on a modulo-256 checksum that must sum to zero, so field reordering, padding changes, or unchecked table contents risk misrouting interrupts.

Raw PCI access is a pair of function pointers for config read and write, each scoped by domain, bus, device-function, register offset and access length, with reads returning status plus a value out-parameter and writes taking a value by value.

Unavailable PCI setup paths are stubbed: direct probing reports failure and direct initialization does nothing, PCBIOS initialization does nothing, and ACPI initialization reports an invalid-argument failure.

An MMCONFIG region entry links into a list, describes its resource and base address, caches a mapped virtual address, identifies segment plus start and end buses, and carries a fixed-size name buffer whose length is defined as 22 plus 4 plus 2 plus 2.
The MMCONFIG bus component of a config address is the bus number shifted left by 20 bits.
MMCONFIG accessors perform width-specific volatile moves for byte, word and dword reads and writes; writes additionally clobber memory so they are ordered against surrounding memory accesses.

Default PCI initialization is configuration-selected: either ACPI setup, legacy setup, or null hooks that disable init, IRQ init and IRQ fixup. One configuration forces the E820-use predicate to false.

Per-CPU addressing selects a segment and relocation style by word size: one configuration uses the GS segment with RIP-relative addressing and another uses FS without it. Assembly and intrinsic forms derive a variable reference, a forced segment prefix, and an optional prefix that is empty in one configuration and forced in the other; address-space qualifiers distinguish the two segments.

The current CPU offset is read from its per-CPU variable. Raw per-CPU pointer formation adds that offset to the input address and reinterprets the sum as a kernel pointer; an alternate configuration unconditionally fails the build and yields a null pointer.

Direct per-CPU access has plain and segment-qualified forms: one exposes the declared type and identity pointer and dereference, while the other qualifies the type with a segment override and converts pointers through an integer before dereference.
Uses an external per-node mask availability predicate owned by another dossier.
Uses an alternate form of an external per-node mask availability predicate owned by another dossier.
